thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - elevated tail latency on streaming endpoints (/v1/chat/stream). p95 ~2.3s, p99 ~24s, streaming.stall_count ↑ 8x. Alerting oncall @lina and ops.

lina: oncall ack. pulling live traces and preproc metrics. which region?

incident-bot: hotspots in ap-southeast preproc pool (inference-preproc-ap) and a few us-east preproc nodes. anomaly window started 1932109600, currently ongoing. No spike in 5xx.

marco: looking at tokenizer/render metrics: template_render_ms p99 = 6300ms on preproc-ap-4, p50 ~140ms. Memory on those pods also elevated; GC churn noted.

devon: grabbing logs. found multiple requests with huge tool schemas plus embedded example arrays. Example: schema_fields_count=420, examples_length=1.2MB. Template engine shows deep recursion on anchors.

priya: that matches recent customer commit patterns - they've switched to 'json-mode' with huge example objects inline. The template engine does full render with example injection for each request. Streaming waits for preproc to finish before first token.

lina: need fast mitigations. Options: (A) immediate gateway-level body-size limit for schema payloads (soft or hard), (B) enable preproc horizontal autoscale + pod restarts, (C) enable degraded streaming path: emit initial tokens ASAP (e.g., system+prefix) while finishing template render in background and patch later, (D) temporarily rewrite templates to placeholders for heavy requests. Quickest to implement?

ops-sre: scaling preproc +4 replicas now. Also evacuating the two oldest pods that show GC thrash.

marco: for (C) we can hack streaming runtime to send a minimal preamble immediately if `render_time_estimate` > 500ms. runtime has code to buffer until preproc returns; toggle is low-risk but needs canary.

devon: canary plan: enable early-preamble streaming on 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% in 20 mins if stable. Need to make sure we can patch the output when final tokens differ due to later template merge. Clients using delta-replace semantics will be fine.

priya: client compatibility note: some SDKs assume monotonic append-only chunks; patching earlier content could confuse them. CS should warn customers.

cs-bot: notifying known customers who had recent large-schema updates. Prepared message: "We detected heavy tool schema payloads causing streaming delays. We may temporarily deliver an initial placeholder stream and then finalize results; please update SDKs to handle token patches or register templates via /templates/create."

lina: for safety also add temporary acceptance policy: requests with schema_size > 1MB will be flagged. Trial-tier accounts will receive 429; enterprise accounts will be allowed but will get `X-Preproc-Mode: background` header. Implemented via feature-flag `schema_size_gate_v1`?

ops-sre: feature-flag rolled out to edge routers. Starting with 20% of traffic. Also scaled preproc and restarted two problematic pods.

marco: logs after changes: 
```
2026-03-14T21:04:12Z preproc INFO req=aa1 render_ms=5120 schema_kb=1180 examples_kb=940 early_preamble_sent=true
2026-03-14T21:04:16Z preproc INFO req=aa2 render_ms=4200 schema_kb=820 examples_kb=620 early_preamble_sent=false
```
marco: early-preamble reduced observed client stall time by ~2.1s for flagged requests. Overall p99 dropped from 24s -> 5.8s on canary traffic.

devon: additional mitigation: strip embedded `examples` arrays larger than 200kb for non-enterprise accounts, replace with comment `<<examples-omitted-size-Xkb>>` to avoid heavy render. That reduces CPU and memory pressure.

lina: agree to accept both measures for short-term: early-preamble streaming + examples stripping for non-enterprise + scale up. Notify SDK teams.

priya: creating short-term telemetry: add metric `template.examples_stripped_total` and `stream.early_preamble_count`. Also add alert: if p99_template_render_ms > 1s for > 10m, fire SRE paging.

devex: client guidance snippet to handle early-preamble: 
```
// SDK should accept 'replace' delta events and re-assemble final message once preproc completes
onDelta(delta) {
  if (delta.type === 'replace') applyReplace(delta);
}
```
cs-bot: sent customer notifications. Two enterprise accounts requested exemption; granted with monitoring and risk review.

ops-sre: scaling and restarts finished. No crashloops observed. CPU tail reduced on preproc-ap nodes.

lina: handoff plan: @marco will watch in 15m, then hand to @devon. Summary for next oncall: root cause = heavy template rendering due to large JSON-mode tool schemas with embedded examples; primary impact = streaming tail stalls; mitigations = scale preproc, early-preamble streaming canary, strip oversized examples for non-enterprise, gateway schema_size gate. Watch metrics: template_render_ms p50/p95/p99, streaming.stall_count, early_preamble_count, template.examples_stripped_total, api.429_schema_rejects.

marco: acknowledged, taking watch. Post-incident action items: (1) implement template render cache keyed by template_id + schema_hash (owner: marco), (2) async template precompute for registered templates + registration API (owner: priya), (3) RFC for streaming runtime to support incremental patching and a contract for SDKs (owner: devex), (4) gate docs and SDK linters to prevent embedding huge examples (owner: devex).

devon: I'm opening follow-up tickets and linking to this thread. Also: investigate memory footprint of template engine; GC tuning might mitigate similar events.

incident-bot: status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity P1. Handoff recorded to marco at 1932110000.

marco: final note: propose adding a pre-ingest lint that warns on `examples` larger than 100kb and suggests `templates/register` usage. I'll draft RFC. Closing this channel in 1 hour unless regressions.

cs-bot: follow-up scheduled with impacted customers; developers will share migration guide and template-registration flow. :white_check_mark:
